- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16), model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates late-period spikes (especially 25–30d horizon) — add 1–3% buffer to forecast tail if sentiment is bullish.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if 10–15d average is trending, forecast should align with 10d moving average rather than 30d.  
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 70+ → 75+) is common — cap forecast at +5% above peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model underestimates rebound — add 1–2% upward correction in 10–15d horizon.
